events.title: The Council of Trent Opens
events.description: Convened by Pope Paul III, the ecumenical council began its sessions in the northern Italian city of Trent. Its purpose was to answer the rapid spread of Protestantism across Europe.
events.significance: Over nearly two decades, the council defined Catholic doctrine and launched sweeping internal reforms. It became the foundation of the Counter-Reformation.

events.title: Francis Drake Sets Sail on His Global Voyage
events.description: Francis Drake left Plymouth, England, aboard the Golden Hind. He was starting a voyage that would take him around the world.
events.significance: Drake's expedition became the second circumnavigation of the globe. It raised England's profile as a rising maritime power.

events.title: Abel Tasman Sights New Zealand
events.description: Dutch explorer Abel Tasman became the first recorded European to see the islands of New Zealand during his voyage across the South Pacific.
events.significance: The sighting placed New Zealand on European maps. Sustained European contact came more than a century later.

events.title: The Battle of Fredericksburg
events.description: Union forces under General Ambrose Burnside attacked entrenched Confederate defenders at Fredericksburg, Virginia, and suffered heavy casualties.
events.significance: It was one of the most lopsided Union defeats of the American Civil War. It deepened the North's crisis of morale in the middle of the conflict.

events.title: The Fall of Nanjing
events.description: Japanese forces entered the Chinese capital of Nanjing. Their arrival began weeks of atrocities against civilians and prisoners of war.
events.significance: The Nanjing Massacre remains one of the darkest episodes of the Second Sino-Japanese War. China now observes December 13 as a national memorial day.
